title.rendered: Be Strong and Courageous — Morning Devotional

excerpt.rendered: God didn’t tell Joshua to feel strong — He commanded him to be strong. Today’s devotional unpacks the difference, and where real courage actually comes from.

content.rendered:
📖 Scripture

“Have I not commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Do not be frightened, and do not be dismayed, for the Lord your God is with you wherever you go.”
— Joshua 1:9 (ESV)

📝 Message

Notice that God did not say: feel strong and courageous. He said: be strong and courageous. The distinction matters enormously.

Feelings are unreliable. Fear is not the absence of faith — it is the presence of a human being confronting something genuinely difficult. Joshua was not a coward. He had walked with Moses for forty years. He had spied out the Promised Land. He had watched God part the Red Sea and rain manna from heaven. And yet here, at the edge of the greatest assignment of his life, God repeated the command three times in the opening chapter alone: Be strong and courageous.

You do not need to command someone who already feels strong. The command reveals the need — and the need reveals the grace behind it.

God was not telling Joshua to manufacture courage from thin air. He was telling him where courage comes from: for the Lord your God is with you wherever you go. The courage is not in your circumstances being manageable. It is not in your abilities being sufficient. It is not in your past record being spotless. It is in the presence of the One who goes with you.

Whatever you are stepping into today — the difficult conversation, the new season, the daunting assignment, the long road of recovery or waiting — hear the same command: Be strong and courageous. Not because you feel ready. But because He goes with you.

You are not going alone. You never were.

🙏 Prayer

Lord, I confess the fear that has been whispering to me about what lies ahead. I choose today to receive Your command as a gift — because You only command what You also enable. You are with me wherever I go. That is enough. Make me strong and courageous not in my own strength, but in Yours. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

🗣️ Declaration

I am strong and courageous — not because my circumstances are easy but because the Lord my God is with me wherever I go. Fear does not have the final word over my life. I step into today with the confidence of a person accompanied by the Most High God. He has commanded my courage and He will supply it.

📖 Further Reading

  • Joshua 1:1–9 — Read the full commissioning of Joshua
  • Deuteronomy 31:6 — Be strong and courageous, do not be afraid
  • Psalm 27:1 — The Lord is my light and my salvation — whom shall I fear?
  • Isaiah 41:10 — Do not fear, for I am with you
  • 2 Timothy 1:7 — God has not given us a spirit of fear
  • Philippians 4:13 — I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me
